concepts.title: Meaning and Importance of Work
concepts.definition: Work is any physical or mental effort directed toward producing a good or performing a service that is useful to oneself or to others.
concepts.key_idea: Work is purposeful effort that creates value for individuals and for society; without work no society can function.
question_patterns: Define work in your own words.
Why is work considered important for society?
Give two examples of work that people do in your neighbourhood.
Distinguish between physical work and mental work with examples.
Explain how work contributes to the well-being of a community.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the activity uses physical or mental effort directed at a goal.
Confirm that the effort produces a good or service of value to oneself or others.
State that because work creates value and meets needs, it is essential for society.

worked_examples.question: Is cooking food for the family considered work? Explain.
worked_examples.solution: Cooking uses physical and mental effort and produces a useful good (food) that meets a basic need, so it qualifies as work.
worked_examples.answer: Yes, cooking food for the family is work because it involves effort and produces something useful.

worked_examples.question: Why is work important for society? Give one reason.
worked_examples.solution: Work produces the goods and services that people need to survive and prosper; without work, needs would go unmet.
worked_examples.answer: Work is important because it creates the goods and services that society depends on.

exercises.question: List three types of work done in your household.
Explain in one sentence why no society can survive without work.

concepts.title: Paid Work
concepts.definition: Paid work is work for which a person receives a wage, salary, or fee in return for the goods produced or services rendered.
concepts.key_idea: Paid work is rewarded with money; the payment may be a fixed salary, a daily wage, or a fee per task.
question_patterns: What is paid work? Give two examples.
How does a wage differ from a salary?
Name three occupations that involve paid work.
Why do people engage in paid work?
Describe one advantage and one challenge of paid work.

solution_steps.explain: Check whether the worker receives money (wage, salary, or fee) for the work done.
Verify that the payment is given in return for goods produced or services rendered.
If both conditions hold, classify the work as paid work.

worked_examples.question: A carpenter makes furniture and is paid Rs 500 per day. Is this paid work?
worked_examples.solution: The carpenter receives a daily wage in return for making furniture, so the work is paid.
worked_examples.answer: Yes, this is paid work because the carpenter receives a wage for the service.

worked_examples.question: Distinguish between a wage and a salary with one example each.
worked_examples.solution: A wage is a payment per day or per task (e.g., a daily-wage labourer), while a salary is a fixed monthly payment (e.g., a teacher).
worked_examples.answer: A wage is paid per day/task; a salary is a fixed monthly payment.

exercises.question: Give two examples of paid work in your locality.
State one reason why people take up paid work.

concepts.title: Voluntary Work
concepts.definition: Voluntary work is work done willingly and without payment for the benefit of the community or a cause.
concepts.key_idea: Voluntary work is driven by a sense of service rather than money; examples include helping during floods or cleaning a park.
question_patterns: What is voluntary work? Give one example.
How does voluntary work differ from unpaid household work?
Describe a situation where voluntary work is important.
Why do people choose to do voluntary work?
List two benefits of voluntary work for a community.

solution_steps.action: Check willingness and absence of pay
solution_steps.explain: Confirm the work is done willingly and without monetary payment.
Verify that the work benefits the community or a cause rather than only oneself.
If both conditions hold, classify the work as voluntary work.

worked_examples.question: Students clean a public park on a holiday without payment. Is this voluntary work?
worked_examples.solution: The students act willingly, receive no money, and benefit the community, so this is voluntary work.
worked_examples.answer: Yes, this is voluntary work because it is unpaid and benefits the community.

worked_examples.question: State one difference between voluntary work and unpaid household work.
worked_examples.solution: Voluntary work benefits the wider community, while unpaid household work mainly benefits one's own family.
worked_examples.answer: Voluntary work serves the community; unpaid household work serves the family.

exercises.question: Give one example of voluntary work in your community.
Explain one benefit of voluntary work for society.

concepts.title: Occupation and Profession
concepts.definition: An occupation is the regular work a person does to earn a living; a profession is an occupation that requires specialised training and knowledge.
concepts.key_idea: All professions are occupations, but not all occupations are professions; professions need formal training and skill.
question_patterns: Define occupation with an example.
Define profession with an example.
How does a profession differ from an occupation?
Is farming an occupation or a profession? Explain.
List three professions and three occupations.

solution_steps.action: Identify the activity and its regularity
solution_steps.explain: Check whether the person does the work regularly to earn a living (occupation).
Determine whether the work requires formal education, training, or a recognised skill.
If specialised training is required, classify it as a profession; otherwise it is an occupation.

worked_examples.question: Is teaching a profession or only an occupation? Justify.
worked_examples.solution: Teaching requires formal training and a qualification, so it is a profession as well as an occupation.
worked_examples.answer: Teaching is a profession because it requires specialised training.

worked_examples.question: Give one example each of an occupation that is a profession and one that is not.
worked_examples.solution: A doctor (profession, needs training) and a street vendor (occupation, no formal training required).
worked_examples.answer: Doctor = profession; street vendor = occupation (not a profession).

exercises.question: List two occupations that are also professions.
State one difference between an occupation and a profession.

concepts.title: Division of Labour
concepts.definition: Division of labour is the splitting of a task into smaller parts, with different people specialising in different parts.
concepts.key_idea: Division of labour increases efficiency and quality because each worker focuses on a specialised part of the task.
question_patterns: What is division of labour? Give one example.
How does division of labour improve efficiency?
Describe division of labour in a restaurant kitchen.
State one advantage and one disadvantage of division of labour.
Explain division of labour with reference to building a house.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the complete task that needs to be accomplished.
Verify that the task is split into parts and different people handle different parts.
State that specialisation leads to greater efficiency and quality.

worked_examples.question: In a garment factory, one person cuts cloth, another stitches, and a third packs. Explain the concept.
worked_examples.solution: The task of making a garment is split among specialists, which is division of labour.
worked_examples.answer: This is division of labour because the task is split among specialised workers.

worked_examples.question: State one advantage of division of labour.
worked_examples.solution: Each worker becomes skilled at one part, so work is done faster and with better quality.
worked_examples.answer: Division of labour increases efficiency and quality.

exercises.question: Give one example of division of labour in a kitchen.
State one disadvantage of division of labour.

concepts.title: Contribution of Workers to Society
concepts.definition: Workers in different fields produce goods and provide services that together meet the needs of society and drive its progress.
concepts.key_idea: Society depends on the combined contribution of farmers, factory workers, teachers, doctors, and many others.
question_patterns: How do farmers contribute to society?
Name two workers who provide services and state their contribution.
Explain how factory workers support daily life.
Why is every worker's contribution important?
Describe how different workers depend on each other.

solution_steps.action: Identify the worker and their output
solution_steps.explain: Determine what good or service the worker produces.

solution_steps.action: Link output to a social need
solution_steps.explain: Connect the good or service to a need of society.
State that the worker's output meets a social need and therefore contributes to society.

worked_examples.question: How does a farmer contribute to society?
worked_examples.solution: A farmer grows food that feeds people, meeting the basic need for nutrition.
worked_examples.answer: A farmer contributes by producing food that society needs to survive.

worked_examples.question: Explain how a teacher's work benefits society.
worked_examples.solution: A teacher educates children, building a skilled and informed future generation.
worked_examples.answer: A teacher contributes by educating the next generation.

exercises.question: Name two workers and state how each contributes to society.
Explain why society depends on many kinds of workers.

concepts.title: Changing Nature of Work
concepts.definition: The nature of work changes over time due to new technology, new needs, and social changes, creating new occupations and reducing some old ones.
concepts.key_idea: Technology and social change create new kinds of work while making some traditional jobs less common.
question_patterns: How has technology changed the nature of work? Give one example.
Name one new occupation that did not exist fifty years ago.
State one traditional occupation that is declining. Why?
How do changing needs of people create new work?
Explain one positive and one negative effect of the changing nature of work.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether technology, new needs, or social change is altering the work.
Check whether new occupations are created or old ones are reduced.
State that the factor has changed the nature of work by creating or reducing occupations.

worked_examples.question: How has the internet created new kinds of work? Give one example.
worked_examples.solution: The internet has created work such as web designing and online teaching that did not exist before.
worked_examples.answer: The internet has created new occupations like web designing.

worked_examples.question: Name one traditional occupation that is declining and suggest a reason.
worked_examples.solution: Handloom weaving is declining because machine-made cloth is cheaper and faster to produce.
worked_examples.answer: Handloom weaving is declining due to competition from machine-made cloth.

exercises.question: Give one example of a new occupation created by technology.
State one way in which changing needs create new work.
